# Keyword Map — Australian Electric Motor Co

*Generated by the keyword-engine skill (hybrid Mode A/B pass) — 2026-09-05. Source: 68 CSV exports
in `keyword exports/` (60 distinct seeds, AU market), double-analysed and unioned (see Methodology).
Supersedes the previous `docs/keyword-map.md` entirely, per your instruction.*

**Re-analysis note (v2):** you were right to ask for a re-check — a "niche relevance" filter I'd
added was too blunt and buried real, huge keywords behind smaller ones, most visibly **"balance
bike" (14,800 vol) was missing from `/shop/balance-mini-bikes/`**, replaced by "electric balance
bike" (1,600). Root cause: I'd built a rule to demote *any* keyword lacking a word like "dirt" or
"electric", meant to catch genuinely ambiguous terms (a bare "bike helmet" or "balaclava" also
serves the bicycle/ski market, not just us) — but it wrongly caught "balance bike" too, which isn't
ambiguous at all; it's the exact, exclusive name of a product we sell. Replaced the blanket rule with
a short, specific list of the actual ambiguous terms, and while re-checking every row by hand found
two more instances of the same root cause (a narrow child category's spike hijacking a *parent* hub's
primary keyword — e.g. `/shop/electric-dirt-bikes/` was showing "balance bike" as **its own** primary
too; and gear-intent keywords like "motocross bike gear" leading a *bike* category page instead of a
bike-buying term). All three fixed and re-read end to end.

**Re-analysis note (v3 — broad scope, no filters):** per your instruction to re-read the exports
without the volume/KD filters for a wider scope, the working set grew from 3,785 keywords to
**15,920** (every unique keyword from every file, no floor, no ceiling, no per-seed cap — see
Methodology). Re-matching that much larger pool surfaced two new instances of the same "shared word,
wrong product" contamination pattern already fixed once in v2:
- **`/shop/front-forks/` and `/shop/rear-shocks/`** were hijacked by Harley-Davidson/Sportster/cafe-racer
  "fork boots"/"shock boots" (a cruiser rubber-gaiter accessory, not a suspension part) — caused by
  those two categories matching on a bare single word (`fork`, `shock`). Tightened both signatures to
  require dirt-bike/suspension context, and added a global exclusion list (Harley, Sportster, Dyna,
  cafe racer, Royal Enfield, Softail, Fatboy, Road King...) checked before any other matching, so it
  can't leak in through a different category or brand either.
- **The RFN (Apollo) brand hub** — "RFN" is also military slang, medical/clinical shorthand, and an EU
  biofuel regulatory acronym (RFNBO), none related to bikes. At the old, filtered scope this never
  surfaced (those terms are all sub-50-volume and got dropped by the floor); at broad scope 9 of them
  appeared on the brand hub's pool ("rfn meaning in army", "rfn medical", "rfn treatment", "rfn
  injection", "rfn spine", "what is rfnbo", "rank rfn"...). Added a matching brand-scoped exclusion list.

Both fixes were verified with a full automated marker scan across every matched page (0 hits) **and**
a complete manual read-through of every category/brand/product row in the regenerated docs — not a
spot-check.

**Primary site keyword:** electric dirt bike → Homepage (`/`) + `/shop/`

## Methodology (what actually happened to the data)

1. **Ingested 68 CSVs.** 6 "duplicate" seed pairs (electric-dirt-bike, balance-bike, ktm, stark-varg,
   surron, talaria) were checked keyword-by-keyword — **they weren't duplicates at all: zero keyword
   overlap between each pair.** Each pair was two complementary exports (one broad-match, one
   question-intent) for the same seed. Both files were unioned, recovering ~380 keywords a naive
   "just pick one" approach would have silently dropped.
2. **Broad-scope pass (v3): no cap, no floor, no ceiling.** The earlier pass capped dirt-bike-boots'
   3 oversized exports (4,100–6,600 rows vs. everyone else's ~100) at 300 rows/seed and dropped
   anything under Vol 50 or over KD 55. Per your instruction, both limits are now removed entirely —
   **15,920 unique keywords** (up from 5,407) go into matching, including everything down to Vol 10.
   A check for high-value-but-hard terms (KD 56+ AND Vol 2,000+) that the old filter might have hidden
   came back empty both before and after removing the cap — confirming the earlier filtered pass
   hadn't buried anything major, just a much longer supporting-keyword tail.
3. **Matched to real, live pages** by brand alias + product-model token + category signature (hand-built
   from the actual 55-category taxonomy) — never to a page that doesn't exist. Two safety nets run
   before any brand/category match is attempted: a **global off-niche exclusion** (cruiser/street-bike
   brands like Harley/Sportster that share a word with a real category — see v3 note above) and a
   **niche-relevance re-rank** that demotes bare high-volume-but-ambiguous terms (e.g. "balaclava"
   22,200 vol, "bike helmet" 8,100 vol) below properly-qualified ones ("dirt bike helmet") on category
   pages, since ranking for the ambiguous term would mean competing in a market we're not in (ski wear,
   bicycles) and wouldn't convert even if achieved. Brand-hub pages are exempt from the ambiguous-term
   re-rank — a bare brand name ("surron", "ktm") is always on-topic — but get their own scoped
   exclusion where the brand name itself is an acronym collision (RFN — see v3 note above).
4. **~50 of 307 real pages got genuine measured keyword data.** The rest (mostly individual product
   pages — 239 of 253) got **zero SKU-specific search volume**, which is normal: nobody searches the
   exact name of a specific spare-part SKU. Those pages use a documented template (see Products
   appendix) rather than fabricated "real" numbers. **10 categories + 1 brand (Kuberg) had zero CSV
   coverage** at broad scope (down from 19 categories at the old, filtered scope — the larger pool
   filled most of the gaps) — supplemented with qualitative research (Google/web related-searches, no
   hard AU volume — marked "(est.)" throughout, never presented as measured). **One category, Linkage
   & Triangles, has neither real nor qualitative data at all** — flagged `NEEDS MANUAL REVIEW` in its
   row below rather than guessed at; it's a genuinely obscure part name (suspension linkage bearings/
   dogbones) that neither the CSV exports nor a quick web check turned up meaningful AU search volume
   for. Worth a manual SEMrush/Google check before Batch 1, or leave it on template-only copy.
5. **Every row below states its own data quality** — "data-backed", "inherited from category/brand +
   template", or "qualitative supplement" — so you can see exactly which assignments are real numbers
   vs. reasoned placeholders before anything gets built.

## Product-gap flag surfaced during this pass

**Alpinestars gear demand: 45,860 combined monthly search volume across 3,739 keyword variants
(alpinestars 5,400 · alpine star 1,900 · alpinestars boots 1,600 · boots alpinestar 1,300 ·
alpinestars helmet 1,300, +3,734 more — figure re-verified at broad scope, up from an earlier
26,900/88-keyword estimate on the filtered pass) — and we have zero dedicated brand presence for it.**
We stock 5 real Alpinestars products (Supertech SM5 helmet, Bionic Action V2 jacket, Tech 3S/Tech 7
boots) scattered across generic categories with no brand grouping, while every *bike* brand (Surron,
Talaria, KTM...) gets its own hub. Same pattern, much smaller, for Fox Racing (60 vol). Full write-up
in `product-gaps.md`.
